dedupe_keys.name: x what open source excel model for looped water distribution network design and optimisation

description: X-WHAT is an open-source Microsoft Excel model to simulate, size and optimise looped water distribution networks under steady-state incompressible flow, presented in a 2024 arXiv paper. Instead of the Hardy Cross method, which needs mass-conservative initial estimates and iterations, it uses the built-in Solver of Excel, needs no mass-conservative starting point and has no flow corrections. The governing equations cover network topology, mass and energy conservation, the cost of tank material and foundation, and the cost of pumping energy to fill the tank. The authors design it for teaching at undergraduate and graduate levels because users can inspect and modify every cell without writing code. Coverage: any small looped network that fits a spreadsheet. Access: the spreadsheet is offered with the paper; the download location and the code licence were not read beyond the abstract; the paper is CC BY 4.0. Caveats: steady-state only, limited to small networks, and not a replacement for full extended-period simulators. It supports network design, optimisation and teaching, and relates to the EPANET model already catalogued.
